name: stegseek - Fast steghide Passphrase Cracker
description: stegseek brute-forces steghide passphrases extremely fast (millions of candidates/sec, ~1000x faster than stegcracker) and auto-extracts the hidden payload on success. It can also detect and recover data without a wordlist in some cases. The go-to tool when a steghide-protected file needs its passphrase broken.
notes:
=== CRACK + AUTO-EXTRACT ===
  stegseek image.jpg /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
  # On success writes image.jpg.out with the hidden payload

=== SPECIFY OUTPUT FILE ===
  stegseek image.jpg rockyou.txt secret.txt

=== SEED/NO-WORDLIST CRACK (empty passphrase payloads) ===
  stegseek --seed image.jpg

=== JUST CHECK FOR A PAYLOAD ===
  stegseek --info image.jpg

=== WHEN TO USE ===
  # After steghide info suggests a payload but the passphrase is unknown
  # Much faster than stegcracker (deprecated) or manual steghide loops

=== FULL IMAGE TRIAGE ===
  exiftool image.jpg
  strings -n 8 image.jpg
  binwalk -e image.jpg
  steghide info image.jpg
  stegseek image.jpg rockyou.txt

recommended.note: steghide embeds/extracts the data stegseek unlocks.

defense.why_it_works: steghide passphrase verification is fast to test offline, and stegseek exploits that to try huge wordlists quickly. Weak/common passphrases fall instantly.
defense.prerequisites: The steghide carrier file; a wordlist.
defense.impact: Recovery of hidden payloads protected by weak passphrases.
defense.detection: Offline attacker-side activity - not detectable on the target.
defense.artifacts: stegseek on the attacker host; .out payload files.
defense.prevention: Use strong, unique passphrases for any steganographic payloads; DLP/steganalysis to catch the carrier before it matters; this is mainly a CTF/offline concern.
